# Security Policy

## Project status

This project is in early development. It has not been deployed and has not been audited by a security professional. Do not use it to process real payments or real customer data.

## Supported versions

Only the latest commit on the default branch is maintained.

## Reporting a vulnerability

Please do not open a public issue for a security problem.

Report privately through GitHub's private vulnerability reporting: open the repository's **Security** tab and choose **Report a vulnerability**. The repository owner must enable this feature under Settings, Code security, once the repository exists on GitHub. Until it is enabled, contact the repository owner directly.

Include:

- What is affected (endpoint, page, or file) and the commit you tested.
- Steps to reproduce, or a proof of concept.
- What an attacker could gain.
- Any suggested fix.

Remove real personal data, passwords, and session tokens from your report.

## What to expect

No response-time commitment is made at this stage of the project. Reports are triaged by severity; the severity scale and the findings register are in [docs/SECURITY.md](../docs/SECURITY.md).

## Scope

In scope: code in this repository and environments operated by the repository owner.

Out of scope: third-party services, denial-of-service testing, social engineering, and testing against any deployment you do not own or have written permission to test.

## Safe harbour

Good-faith research that stays in scope, avoids privacy violations and service disruption, and gives reasonable time to fix before disclosure is welcome.
